subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox pruning can remove a runtime refreshed after its stale snapshot

question: Should graceful sandbox pruning be serialized through the owning Gateway, or through a process-shared recoverable lifecycle lease?
rationale: Current process-local coordination cannot protect separate processes, and this choice defines crash recovery, hung-work behavior, and the sandbox mutation security boundary.

options.title: Gateway-owned pruning
options.body: Route graceful prune through the owning Gateway so one lifecycle process drains work and performs fresh runtime and registry checks.

options.title: Recoverable shared lease
options.body: Implement a process-shared lease with stale-owner recovery plus runtime-identity and registry-version compare-and-swap checks.

recommendation.title: Gateway-owned pruning
recommendation.body: Route graceful prune through the owning Gateway so one lifecycle process drains work and performs fresh runtime and registry checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail and recent adjacent lifecycle work make this the strongest evidence-backed decision owner.
